title: Lunar AeroLabs Reveals Advanced LAGF800 Avionics and Flight Management Systems for MSFS 2024
summary: Lunar AeroLabs showcases advanced LAGF800 avionics for MSFS 2024, including detailed FMS flight planning, VNAV, EICAS, navigation displays and landing-performance calculations.
body:
Lunar AeroLabs has released an extensive new development update showcasing the advanced avionics being created for its upcoming LAGF800 ultra-long-range business jet for Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024.

Shared by developer CaptainLunar through the project's official Discord server, the announcement provides a detailed look at the aircraft's Flight Management System (FMS), navigation displays, systems monitoring and landing-performance functionality.

Accompanied by a collection of development screenshots, the update highlights the developer's ambition to create a fully integrated flight deck rather than simply reproduce the appearance of modern business jet avionics.

## Advanced Flight Management System

![](</assets/2026-11-08 Image 4.png>)

One of the main areas highlighted in the announcement is the LAGF800's Flight Management System.

According to Lunar AeroLabs, the FMS is being developed to support detailed flight planning and management throughout a flight.

The functionality described includes:

- Advanced waypoint information, route sequencing and flight predictions.
- Altitude and speed constraints.
- Vertical navigation data, including vertical speed, flight-path angles and calculated altitude profiles.
- Flight progress monitoring, including groundspeed, wind conditions, atmospheric information and navigation accuracy.
- Multiple selectable flight-plan layouts.
- Direct-to navigation, route amendments and holding patterns.
- Airway insertion and crossing restrictions.

These features are intended to provide pilots with detailed control over both lateral and vertical flight planning.

The developer's screenshots show flight-plan pages displaying route information, navigation data and individual waypoint details.

## Navigation and Situational Awareness

![](</assets/2026-11-08 Image 1.png>)

Lunar AeroLabs is also developing an integrated navigation environment combining aircraft positioning, flight-plan information and geographical awareness.

The latest previews demonstrate terrain mapping, flight-plan visualisation, waypoint information and navigation overlays.

Importantly, the developer describes synchronisation between the main avionics displays and touchscreen controllers.

This integration is intended to allow information entered or modified through the flight-management interface to be reflected across the flight deck.

For pilots operating complex long-range routes, the ability to manage and monitor flight information across multiple displays could become an important part of the aircraft's operational experience.

## Aircraft Systems and EICAS

![](</assets/2026-11-08 Image 8.png>)

The development update also provides further information about the LAGF800's aircraft systems monitoring.

Lunar AeroLabs describes an integrated Engine Indicating and Crew Alerting System (EICAS), together with selectable pages covering several aircraft systems.

These include:

- Live engine indications and performance parameters.
- Fuel quantities and system monitoring.
- Hydraulic pressure indications.
- Brake temperatures and brake demand.
- Flight-control monitoring.
- Environmental systems.
- Camera interfaces.

The developer's intention is to integrate these systems directly into the flight deck, allowing pilots to monitor aircraft conditions through dedicated avionics pages.

The screenshots provide an early indication of how these interfaces are being organised, although their appearance and functionality remain subject to development.

## Detailed Landing Performance and Arrival Management

![](</assets/2026-11-08 Image 2.png>)

One of the most interesting elements of the announcement concerns the aircraft's arrival and landing interfaces.

The developer has showcased a dedicated landing-performance page incorporating runway information, approach-speed calculations and landing configuration data.

The functionality described includes:

- Landing runway and available-distance information.
- VREF and approach-speed calculations.
- Landing weight and configuration information.
- Autobrake selection.
- Barometric minimums.
- Altimeter settings.
- Landing-data confirmation and dispatch interfaces.

One screenshot shows a landing-performance calculation for Denver International Airport, including runway selection, reference speeds, aircraft landing weight and autobrake settings.

This represents an interesting level of detail for a business jet add-on, particularly if the various performance calculations are successfully integrated with the aircraft's flight-management and systems simulation.

## Software-Driven Avionics

![](</assets/2026-11-08 Image 5.png>)

Lunar AeroLabs has also emphasised that the displays shown are not simply static cockpit textures or decorative graphics.

According to CaptainLunar, the avionics are being developed using software technologies including HTML, CSS and JavaScript, alongside aircraft systems integration.

The developer states that the displays interact with flight-management functions and aircraft systems using real-time data.

This approach is intended to create an interconnected avionics environment in which flight-planning inputs, navigation information and aircraft systems work together.

Although the screenshots provide a useful indication of the project's progress, the developer acknowledges that further refinement and testing remain necessary.

## Development Continues

The LAGF800 remains under active development, with Lunar AeroLabs indicating that many additional avionics pages, interactions and capabilities have yet to be revealed.

The developer has previously discussed a target release window in 2027, although no firm launch date has been confirmed in this latest announcement.

CaptainLunar has emphasised that the priority is to create an aircraft that is rewarding to learn and operate rather than rushing development to meet a particular deadline.

The latest screenshots should therefore be regarded as work-in-progress material, with features and interfaces subject to further refinement.

![](</assets/2026-11-08 Image 6.png>)

## BizJet Pilot's View

The latest LAGF800 development update is particularly encouraging for enthusiasts interested in complex business jet operations.

While detailed exterior modelling and passenger cabins contribute to immersion, it is the depth and integration of the flight-management and aircraft systems that often determine how rewarding an aircraft is to operate over the longer term.

The inclusion of detailed vertical flight planning, navigation management, EICAS functionality and landing-performance calculations suggests that Lunar AeroLabs is placing considerable emphasis on the operational side of its ultra-long-range business jet.

The screenshots are promising, although the ultimate depth, accuracy and reliability of these systems will only become clear as development and testing progress.

BizJet Pilot will continue following the project as further avionics demonstrations and development milestones are announced.
